Wang et al. 2610.06851, read in full (papers/arxiv-2610.06851.txt). (1) Their RL model is allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release, per their repo), not our Olmo-3.1. On MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / cap 31,744, 32 rollouts: base 42.2 -> cue 77.9 (Table 5); RL 75.0 -> 75.3 with cue (Table 6). So on their pair the cue already equals RL on MATH-500; our 10.6-point gap is against 3.1 only and is not in the paper. (2) DIRECTION.md says they report 77.7 for the cue: Table 5 says 77.9; 77.7 is the row 'RL opening + base continuation' (Table 13). (3) Their cue is 2 tokens ('.\n\n' + 'Okay'), chosen without labels by lowest answer entropy on 30 MATH train problems. (4) Cued base pass@16 on MATH-500 = 95.4 (Table 5), above our RL pass@1 of 92.6: the missing points are in the base's samples. (5) Harder sets: RL leads the cued base by 5-12 points (AMC 23 66.2 vs 59.5, AIME 2024 35.2 vs 23.3, OlympiadBench 41.6 vs 36.5), unexplained in the paper. (6) Not in the paper: any temperature sweep, restarts, base + a*(RL - base), a Code-RL model. 0 citing papers indexed on 2026-11-14. (7) Olmo 3 report 2512.13961 A.6.4: 3.1 differs from 3.0 by completion length 16k instead of 12k and by not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives). work-2aaf3a

Published, do not run on a plain base (papers read in full, texts in papers/): (a) power sampling / MCMC: +2.4 to +3.5 points on MATH-500, 18-27 % of the RL gain, none on AIME (2610.24663 Table 1). (b) Fixed rules: forced 'Wait', logit bias, greedy first 100 tokens, entropy stop, longer prefill: at or below base (2610.24663 Tables 3, 5, App. G). (c) Majority vote: plain base stays below RL for 24 of 24 decoding policies at every N up to 16 on Qwen2.5-7B / MATH-500 (2609.01274 Fig. 8b). Maj@4 adds 0.8 points to a 73.6 % model on MATH500; best-of-n by self-confidence is below one sample (2507.18122 Table 1). (d) Loop penalties: DRY costs 14.2 points on MATH-500 for Qwen3-4B (2610.24715 Table 16). (e) Top-p vs temperature: removing top-p at T 0.6 cuts limit loops 59 -> 53, T 1 cuts to 24 (Qwen3-4B, 360 structured generations, not math; 2610.24715 Table 9). (f) RL gain is sparse: RL's greedy token at the 4 % of positions where greedy tokens differ recovers 90.5 % of the gain on AIME; base entropy finds those positions with AUROC 0.94-0.98; RL's token has mean rank 2.1-2.4 in the base (2610.24663 Table 3, App. E; 2605.06241 Table 2). No label-free rule is published that picks the right token there. (g) Label-free training (entropy minimization, vote reward) closes 80-100 % of the gap on Math-500 and 0-70 % on AIME for Qwen2.5-Math-7B (2505.15134 Table 2); vote reward collapses near 1,000 steps (2603.08660). None of (a)-(g) was run on a cued base or on the Olmo pair. work-2aaf3a

Goodfire 'Neurons as an Interpretable Basis' (Nov 10 2026, goodfire.com/research/neurons-as-an-interpretable-basis), read in full by a subagent. Table 1/8 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, SwiGLU): keeping only the top 320 of 4,096 routed MLP neuron activations per token and layer, with no training, raises loss 1.886 -> 1.940 (+2.9%) and raises MATH-500 from 69.8 by +5.8 (top-64: +7.0; resample noise +0.8) at a 4,096 thinking-token cap. Accuracy on items both arms finished is flat, so the gain is more answers finishing under the cap (subagent's inference). Other evals fell (GPQA-Diamond -11 to -18, MBPP+ -20) from looping and excess self-checking. Fig. 4: ablating all Q3 activations (gate<0 and up<0) cut GSM8K reasoning 1,550 -> 176 tokens. Single neurons control 'settle vs keep questioning' (L9_E98_N330). Their small RL recalibration 'mainly taught the model to commit and stop'. Not in the paper: any base-vs-fine-tune diff, any weight edit, any model near 7B. No code released.

From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 loop detectors): use the zlib rule (rule A), not a period rule or a repeated-line count, to call base-model loops. Rule A: an 8,000-character window starting at a line start with zlib compression ratio < 0.10; onset = first line of the repeated block. Tested on saved MATH-500 answers (T 0.6, cap 16,384): fires on 0 of 484 RL finished answers, 1 of 431 base plain (n13), 0 of 435 and 0 of 381 for two base-01 cells; fires on 59 of 60, 46 of 48 and 90 of 92 low-ratio cap hits. Rule B (period <= 64 characters over >= 2,000 characters, 3 cycles; as relayed from arXiv 2611.06095, paper not read) has no false positives but catches only 6-17 % of the loops, because the base's loops have periods of hundreds of characters. A crude rule (any line > 20 characters three times) fires on 60 of 484 RL finished answers, so it fails. Caveat: on low-ratio cap hits rule A's hit rate is nearly guaranteed by construction; the test is the false-positive side, and the onset was checked by eye on 4 answers only. At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3 (500 each); the cued base at T 0.6 has 92 low-ratio cap hits of 119. Status: closed instrument check, not audited.
